lines: 1 package is imported by their root in src, so the whole barrel is reachable and the bundler keeps whatever it cannot prove unused:

@nextcloud/vue: 1,687,351 B in 225 modules, 40.7 % of the static path of crate-main.js, imported by its root in 20 files: App.vue (NcAppContent, NcAppNavigation, NcAppNavigationItem, ...), components/AddEditModal.vue (NcButton, NcModal), and 18 more.
Importing the module that is used instead of the package root lets the bundler drop the rest of the barrel.
ncmake's lint-vue-imports workflow gates exactly this specifier for @nextcloud/vue, so this finding is that red check with a byte figure attached.

61 components of @nextcloud/vue are delivered although no file in src names them, no other dependency names them and no component named by either imports them: 227,664 B, 5.5 % of the static path of crate-main.js, next to 11 components the source names, 3 that other dependencies name and 6 those pull in.
NcRichText 49,551 B, NcDateTimePicker 47,492 B, NcProfileHoverCard 15,086 B, NcAvatar 12,781 B, NcAppSidebar 10,584 B, NcSelect 7,154 B, and 55 more.
These arrive through the root import: under a barrel the whole component set is reachable, so the bundler must keep it. Per-component imports leave it free to drop what the app never names.

111 delivered files look like a webpack or CommonJS bundle. Their internal structure is not derivable from the artefact, so each counts as one file and the chunk figures below say nothing about what is inside them.
Every delivered file in js carries a source map, so every byte can be charged to the package and the module it came from.
